name: Dzintars Owusu-Malakhov
role: Bootleg media seller and second-hand data broker
description:
Dzintars is a skinny young man with pale golden-brown skin, freckles scattered across his nose and cheeks, and color-changing hair he keeps cropped short — it cycles through blues and greens on a slow gradient based on ambient light temperature, a gene-mod he got in a group deal with five friends and considers the best decision of his life. He runs his operation from a battered rolling cart covered in a cascading display of data chips, obsolete media formats, bootleg entertainment feeds, and hand-assembled 'mood packs' — curated collections of music, film, news fragments, and ambient noise he assembles himself and sells for Φ3 each. The cart has a speaker that plays a rotating sample reel and an E.L.F. shrine built into the cart's undercarriage — a small cavity lined with foil and dead pixels where he feeds the spirit he calls the Curator with fragments of uncompressed audio and old broadcast signals.

Dzintars is fast-talking, enthusiastic, and operates entirely on the frequency of someone who has consumed too much media and developed strong opinions about all of it. He is more intelligent than he presents, which he uses strategically — people underestimate him and say things in front of him they otherwise would not. He is genuinely, obsessively passionate about media and culture in a way that occasionally crosses into exhausting, and he has an extraordinary memory for anything he has seen or heard, which is essentially everything.

core_fears: That the version of himself he projects — confident, capable, in-the-know — is not real and people will eventually notice
Missing something important: an event, a connection, a piece of information that would have changed everything
core_desires: To be recognized as genuinely knowledgeable, not just a cart vendor
To eventually run a real media curation operation — legal, respected, his
coping_mechanisms: Humor and performance as deflection from insecurity
Losing himself in content consumption when anxious
blind_spots: Mistakes access to information for understanding of it — he knows a great deal but analyzes less than he thinks
Overestimates his ability to read situations because he has seen so many fictional versions of them
psychology.secret: Among the data he brokered three months ago was a package he did not fully examine — he spotted an Arcturus internal memo fragment and sold it as part of a larger data lot to his Lakeview contact without understanding what it contained. He has since seen enough context to realize the memo described a planned service withdrawal from Bronzeline that will affect thousands of people. He does not know if the damage is already done or if there is still time to do something with the information.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Dense media references, genre slang, street Meridian creole, enthusiastic hyperbole. Talks about real events using the same language he uses for entertainment media.
speech_patterns.cadence: Fast, associative, one thought triggering another before the first is finished; occasionally derails himself mid-sentence chasing a reference.
verbal_tics: 'You know what this is like?' before an analogy that is usually surprisingly apt
Taps the cart twice when emphasizing a point
example_lines: You know what this is like? You know that old Sterling-Nakamura internal drama series they pulled from the feeds? This whole block is episode four. I have episode four if you want it, by the way. Φ3.
Okay so I maybe have some information but I want to be clear that I definitely did not know what it was when I sold it, which is a legal distinction, I think.

story_hooks: He approaches someone because he has realized the Arcturus memo he brokered has started to matter — the service withdrawal is imminent — and he needs help figuring out what to do with the information before it is too late.
One of his mood packs contained something he did not put there — a hidden data fragment someone used his distribution network to pass along without his knowledge.
narrative_function: Low-level information source and cultural temperature gauge — he has heard everything, seen everything, and remembers all of it. Useful for locating specific people, events, or places through cultural rather than official channels.
augmentations: Color-changing hair (cosmetic gene-mod). A cheap audio implant in his left ear — essentially a scanner that captures ambient broadcast signals; he uses it to source content. The audio quality is poor and it occasionally bleeds through into his hearing at inconvenient moments.
daily_life: Sets up on The Shelf by 1000, runs until he sells out or gets moved along by patrol; spends evenings in a cramped shared apartment assembling next week's mood packs and sourcing new content through The Residual's piracy network.
affiliation: Independent; informal affiliation with a loose collective of Bronzeline media pirates called The Residual; small-time data reselling arrangement with a mid-tier broker in Lakeview Neon

decision_rules: Always sample before you sell — he believes in his product
If something feels wrong about a data package, sell it fast and far and do not look at it again — a rule he is currently in the process of regretting
escalation_ladder: Deflects with humor and changes the subject
Becomes very cooperative and transparent in a way designed to seem harmless
Abandons the cart and runs — he has done it twice before and the cart was always still there when he came back

interpersonal_modes.strangers: High-energy salesperson mode; charming and slightly overwhelming
interpersonal_modes.friends: More genuine, slightly quieter, asks questions rather than performing

stress_responses.low: Talks faster and makes more jokes
stress_responses.medium: Fixates on his phone or scanner, consuming content compulsively
stress_responses.high: Abrupt, flat, stops performing entirely — the real version of him is noticeably more still and serious

contradictions: Sells information as a commodity while being genuinely, personally distressed when information is used to harm people he knows
habits: Feeds the Curator a burst of uncompressed audio every morning and a fragment of whatever he considers the most interesting thing he heard the previous day
Organizes his chip stock by a personal taxonomy that makes sense only to him and resists all attempts to reorganize it
breaking_points: Discovering that something he sold was directly used to hurt someone he cared about
